correctness.rationale: For each n>=2, K>1, alpha threshold, the 2n precommitted short/long inputs share n-1 unit goods and target-specific special goods. At alpha<=1/K a deterministic initial distinct prefix and final allocation attains all inputs. At alpha>1/K every successful short input requires an injective prefix; with unique empty recipient b, a=b admits both horizons, and each a!=b admits at most one. Optimal deterministic response to arbitrary prior q therefore equals max_b(q_bS+q_bL+sum_(a!=b) max(q_aS,q_aL)). Writing r_a=q_aS+q_aL and d_a=|q_aS-q_aL| gives F=(1+D+max_b(r_b-d_b))/2>= (n+1)/(2n), with equality uniquely at uniform q. Uniform b and a coin in the mismatch give exact pointwise equalizer; deterministic minmax zero at high alpha. Independent rational finite-game enumeration for n=2,3 and nonuniform priors matched.

originality.rationale: The 2n hard-instance family is identical to Chen–Long Section 4.2, but their published upper bound for unrestricted online input sequences is different from proving attainable minimax on only this subfamily with unique dual solution. The uniform-prior upper bound alone neither proves a restricted-family saddle point nor forces uniqueness across arbitrary input priors; the threshold at alpha=1/K is another separate statement. The claim is a limited, credited refinement of the same model. Best-of-knowledge priority risk remains explicit; unsuccessful search alone is not claimed as proof of novelty.
residual_risks: Chen–Long full text was not available for inspection; their proof of the SAME hard family may implicitly contain a stronger equilibrium/unique-distribution argument than its summarized theorem. This is a material priority risk, not a claim of complete exclusion.
Only the explicitly fixed finite 2n-input adversary is solved; no unrestricted online randomized EF1 guarantee is asserted.
